module_title: Demographic Trends, Union Territories, and the Great Divide
introduction: At this level, we will analyze the extreme statistics of Union Territories (UTs) and districts. We will also explore the historical milestones in Indian demographics, specifically the year that permanently altered India's population trajectory.

core_concepts.title: The Year of Great Divide (1921)
core_concepts.description: In India's demographic history, the year '1921' is termed the 'Year of the Great Divide'. During the 1911-1921 decade, India's population growth rate was actually 'negative' (-0.31%) due to severe famines and the Spanish Flu pandemic. After 1921, India's population never declined; it grew continuously and rapidly.

core_concepts.title: Population Density of Union Territories
core_concepts.description: If we include Union Territories, 'Delhi' (NCT) has the absolute highest population density in all of India (a staggering 11,320 persons/sq km). The UT with the lowest population density is the 'Andaman & Nicobar Islands' (46 persons/sq km).

core_concepts.title: District-Level Extremes
core_concepts.description: The most densely populated district in India is 'North East Delhi'. On the other end, the least densely populated district in India is 'Dibang Valley' in Arunachal Pradesh, which has a density of exactly 1 person per square kilometer.

core_concepts.title: The Period of Population Explosion (1951-1981)
core_concepts.description: The decades from 1951 to 1981 are referred to as the period of 'population explosion' in India. This was caused by a massive and sudden drop in the Mortality (Death) Rate due to better healthcare, while the Fertility (Birth) Rate remained exceptionally high.

important_entities.name: Kerala
important_entities.significance: Among the states that actually grew (excluding Nagaland), Kerala recorded the lowest decadal growth rate (just 4.9%). This is a direct consequence of Kerala's high literacy rate, excellent healthcare system, and strong women's empowerment initiatives.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a question explicitly asks: 'Which State/UT has the highest population density in India?' the answer is 'Delhi' (not Bihar). Always scan the options. Only choose Bihar if the question strictly specifies 'State'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Delhi = Highest UT Density. Andaman & Nicobar = Lowest UT Density.

exam_strategy_tips: The '1921 Year of Great Divide' is a classic, guaranteed question in SSC, Railways, and State PCS exams.

In Assertion-Reasoning questions, note that the 'Population Explosion' (1951-1981) was NOT caused by people having *more* babies, but by a sudden decline in the *death rate* due to medical advancements.
